To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the dendrites of layer 4 spiny cells are innervated by both thalamic afferents and by axon collaterals from layer 4 cells, (b) the dendrites are innervated in a manner that is consistent with a feed-forward and a lateral inhibition model for the receptive field, and (c) dendritic inhibition can help to maintain orientation sensitivity in the face of luminance changes.

the orientation selectivity of a cortical cell depends on the strength of its excitatory inputs, that the orientation tuning of a cortical cell is determined by the orientation tuning of its excitatory input neurons, and that the orientation tuning and contrast gain control of a cortical cell are determined by the strength of its inhibitory inputs.

(1) the dendritic arbors of cortical cells are organized to sample the receptive fields of thalamic cells; (2) the dendrites of cortical cells receive input from multiple thalamic cells that have similar receptive fields; and (3) these two features, dendritic sampling and dendritic convergence, together help to maintain orientation sensitivity in cortical cells when the contrast of the visual scene fluctuates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the cellular and circuit mechanisms that underlie visual cortical processing.
the neural circuits that build the receptive field structure of cortical neurons and that maintain neural sensitivity to visual features even when stimulus contrast changes.
the mechanisms by which the brain builds and maintains receptive field structure, and the role of these receptive fields in the perception of visual form.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the simple cell is a cortical invention, and the thalamus is the source of the information needed for this invention.
simple cells are not as simple as once thought, and that the mechanisms that build their receptive fields remain elusive.

we do not know how simple cells are built, but we have learned a lot about the basic principles and the general mechanisms that underlie the formation of simple cells and the maintenance of their sensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cortical neurons are not passive recipients of information from the thalamocortical afferents, but actively shape their own responses by modifying their synaptic input.
cortical circuits are organized to build receptive field structure and to maintain neural sensitivity in the presence of contrast.
simple cells in cat V1 are the product of a circuit that combines excitatory and inhibitory inputs from thalamic and cortico-cortical sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the receptive fields of simple cells are built from a combination of thalamic and cortical inputs.
the visual cortex is not a homogeneous tissue, but rather that there are distinct subpopulations of cells, each with their own receptive fields.
the visual cortex contains many types of neurons with different functional properties, but the same circuit motifs are used to generate them.
